classification.difficultyReason: Find an unlabelled triangle side using intersecting chord products, then use that intermediate length in Pythagoras to obtain the requested hypotenuse.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Perpendicular intersecting vertical and horizontal chords, with a diagonal chord joining the bottom and right endpoints. Ordinary source colours are replaced by house black.
spec.mathematics: The vertical intercepts are 3 cm and 8 cm; the left horizontal intercept is 4 cm. The right horizontal intercept is unlabelled. The diagonal chord is x. All four endpoints lie on the circle, and the intersecting chords meet at a right angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and x are visible; the supplied 10 cm answer is omitted.

answer.worked:
Let the right horizontal intercept be $h$ cm. The products of the intercepts of intersecting chords are equal.
$$\begin{align*}4h&=3\times8\\4h&=24\\h&=6\end{align*}$$
By Pythagoras in the right-angled triangle,
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=8^2+6^2\\x^2&=100\\x&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
